title: What If Nobody Could Lie? 🌀 Swirlverse
description:
Kiko made soup. Nova was honest. Ouch. 🍲
In our world, most of us tell white lies every day. But science says it's not who you think: most people tell no lies on a given day, and a small group tells almost half of them. And can you spot a liar? Barely better than a coin flip.
In this parallel world, nobody can lie. Not even a tiny white lie. Honest ads, very short job interviews, excuses that don't work... and a judge who just asks "did you do it?"

Would you want a world with no lies? Tell me in the comments!

Facts in this video:
• Diary study: college students told about 2 lies a day, about 1 lie in every 3 social interactions (community members: about 1 a day, 1 in 5 interactions). (DePaulo et al., 1996)
• Survey of 1,000 U.S. adults: 60% reported telling no lies at all on a given day; almost half of all reported lies came from just 5% of people ("prolific liars"). (Serota, Levine & Boster, 2010)
• Across 206 studies (24,483 judges), people correctly judged lies vs truths 54% of the time; guessing gives 50%. (Bond & DePaulo, 2006)
• Children begin telling lies around age 2–3; researchers link it to developing theory of mind (understanding that others know and think differently) and self-control. (Evans & Lee, 2013; Talwar & Lee, 2008)
